Pseudo-out-of-sample diagnostic - revised data - not a real-time vintage study

Variable importance and large-error diagnostics

Impact is measured in percentage points of real seasonally adjusted quarterly GDP growth (100 x log difference). Bridge impacts are an exact additive decomposition conditional on each fitted window. DFM impacts neutralize one contemporaneous indicator at a time; they are marginal, correlated-system effects and not causal estimates.

Largest forecast mistakes

Positive error means underestimation; negative error means overestimation. The diagnostic is descriptive and can identify inertia, wrong direction, COVID regime breaks, and indicators that pushed the estimate away from the realization.

How to interpret

Selection frequency is stability, not impact. Mean absolute impact answers how much a variable moved predictions across all test forecasts. Helped means the full forecast had a smaller absolute error than the same forecast with that variable neutralized. A variable can be economically important and still hurt during a regime break. The analysis uses current revised data and therefore does not reproduce historical release vintages.
